model_reported.summary: This experiment uses the CUDA runtime and CUB BlockReduce already present in the source and introduces no architecture-specific instruction or resource assumption.

model_reported.summary: No new API or uncertain compiler or hardware behavior is required; the candidate retains the existing CUDA reset, launch, and CUB reduction pattern.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared the visible valid outcomes without attributing their differences to a single cause; this candidate still needs total-time measurement and official validation.

memory_lessons.applicability: These are complete-program measurements; the compared candidates differed in more than CTA cap, so they motivate but do not predict this result.
memory_lessons.claim: The visible T2 results report 0.3436 ms for the 512-cap four-accumulator candidate, 0.4474 ms for the 1024-cap single-accumulator candidate, and 1.5543 ms for the 256-cap single-accumulator candidate. All were marked correct and valid.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 384-cap four-accumulator variant against the 512-cap candidate with reset and launch overhead included, then validate every required case.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured 512-CTA, four-accumulator program was faster than the visible 256-CTA and 1024-CTA alternatives, though those results do not isolate CTA count. A 384-CTA cap with the same four-way per-thread accumulation tests whether reducing CTA atomics from 512 can retain enough parallelism for large inputs. Each call still resets output before one input pass and one atomic per CTA; compare total time and validate all required sizes and FP64 tolerance.

retained: Keep the per-call asynchronous output reset in the default stream before launching the reduction; do not depend on scratch contents.
Stream input once, accumulating four grid-stride positions independently per thread before one CUB block reduction and one output atomicAdd per CTA.
Choose ceil(n/256) CTAs for smaller inputs and cap the grid at 384 CTAs for larger inputs.
